source.title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB, and more generally for paraparticle (co)algebras of the kind discussed in the paper, which gradings by small finite abelian groups G (for example Z2, Z3, Z4, or Z2 × Z2) preserve the algebra and coalgebra structures? Equivalently, classify the group actions or coactions that turn these paraparticle (co)algebras into G-(co)module (co)algebras.

evidence.quote: 1st Research Objective: The first problem we intend to investigate is the classification of the gradings induced on the paraparticle (co)algebras (especially on PBF and PFB algebras) by small order finite Abelian Groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, Z2 × Z2 etc. In other words, we intend to classify those group (co)actions which preserve the corresponding (co)algebra structures, turning thus the (co)algebras in G-(co)module (co)algebras.

accepted.question_text: Once a grading of the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF or PFB by a finite abelian group G is fixed, what braided group structures are compatible with that grading? In particular, for a given grading one wants to classify the admissible bicharacters, equivalently the corresponding universal R-matrices and braidings, determine whether the known Z2 × Z2 grading of PBF is compatible with commutation factors other than the standard one used in the cited works, and decide which of these braided structures arise from an underlying colored G-graded Lie structure via a universal enveloping algebra construction.

evidence.quote: Given the (Z2 × Z2)-grading described in [14,15,34,35] we intend to check whether it is compatible with other commutation factors θ (i.e.,: other braidings for the (Z2 × Z2)M Category of modules) than the one presented in these works. In other words, we are going to determine possible alternative braided group structures, corresponding to the single (Z2 × Z2)-graded structure for PBF described in the above works.

2nd Research Objective: Further, for each of the above gradings we intend to classify the corresponding braided group structures. In other words, we will write down the possible bicharacters of the above groups or equivalently the possible R-matrices of the corresponding group Hopf algebras or equivalently the braidings of the corresponding Category CGM (or MCG) of modules (or comodules).

accepted.question_text: Can one apply or develop bosonization, or a bosonization-like construction, that converts the graded and braided Hopf structures attached to these paraparticle algebras into ordinary Hopf algebras with trivial braiding while preserving the representation theory up to equivalence?

evidence.quote: 3rd Research Objective: Apply or develop suitable bosonization or bosonization-like techniques to obtain ordinary Hopf structures, with no grading and with trivial braiding, possessing equivalent representation theories.

accepted.question_text: Using the braided-tensor-product method sketched in the paper, can one explicitly construct the Fock-like representations of the infinite-degree-of-freedom parabosonic algebra PB and parafermionic algebra PF? For PB in particular, this requires developing a mathematically usable multinomial theorem for the anticommuting variables that appear in the tensor-product realization, computing the generator action explicitly, decomposing the resulting graded tensor-product representations into irreducible components, and determining whether the decomposition contains irreducible summands other than the known p-Fock-like modules.

evidence.quote: We first intend to proceed to the explicit construction of the Fock-like representations in the case of the (inf. deg. of freedom) parabosonic PB and parafermionic PF algebra following the methodology developed in [103] and outlined above.

The mathematical problem here, which is necessary to be solved in order to explicitly perform the computation is the development of a suitable multinomial theorem in the anticommuting variables (b_i^+)^(k).

In [103] we have proved that the p-Fock-like modules are contained as irreducible factors of such graded, tensor product representations. However, it remains to see whether such decompositions can produce as direct summands or more generally as submodules other non-equivalent representations as well.

accepted.question_text: Can the braided-tensor-product method for explicit representation construction be generalized from PB and PF to the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB by using the algebras Ws and Was as suitable graded quotients and then extracting Fock-like representations as irreducible submodules of graded tensor-product representations? A key unresolved subproblem is to develop a suitable multinomial theorem that simultaneously handles commuting and anticommuting variables in this mixed setting.

evidence.quote: The next step will consist of generalizing the above calculations for the case of the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB. The philosophy of the method is based on the same idea: The Fock-like representations of PBF and PFB will be extracted as irreducible submodules arising in the decomposition of the graded tensor product representations of Ws and Was.
Finally it is worth mentioning, that the computational problem we expect to reveal here is the development of a suitable multinomial theorem mixing commuting and anticommuting variables.
However, the general cases of PBF, PFB, SBF and SFB algebras remain still open (even in the case of the finite degrees of freedom).

accepted.question_text: Is there a family of exactly solvable quantum models generalizing the Jaynes-Cummings system in which a monochromatic parabosonic field interacts with a (p + 1)-level system, with spectrum-generating algebra chosen from mixed paraparticle algebras such as PBF(1,1), PFB(1,1), SCR(1,1), or SAR(1,1)? More specifically, can one construct such Hamiltonians, compute energy levels, eigenfunctions, and transition rates from the associated Fock-like representations, and compare conventional interaction-term quantization with algebraic or statistical quantization in which the interaction is encoded in the algebraic relations themselves rather than explicit Hamiltonian interaction terms?

evidence.quote: Using the Fock-like modules described above, we will attempt to proceed in a generalization of the above model in the study of the interaction of a monochromatic parabosonic field with a (p + 1)-level system.

In this way, we will actually construct a family of exactly solvable, quantum mechanical models, whose properties will be studied quantitatively (computation of energy levels, eigenfunctions, rates of transitions between states, etc.) and directly compared with theoretical and experimental results.

Last, but not least, it is expected that the study of such models will provide us with deep insight into the process of Quantization itself: We will be able to proceed in direct comparison between mainstream quantization methods of Quantum Mechanics ... and the idea of Algebraic (or Statistical) Quantization ...
